summary: Casa De Campo International Airport (LRM) serves the southeastern Dominican Republic, primarily catering to guests of the world-renowned Casa de Campo resort complex. Located just minutes from La Romana and the resort's famous Teeth of the Dog golf course, the airport handles a mix of scheduled and seasonal charter flights mainly from North America. Its compact terminal and quick processing times make it a popular alternative to the busier airports in Punta Cana and Santo Domingo.
faqs:
Q: How far is Casa De Campo International Airport from the Casa de Campo resort?
A: The airport is approximately 5-10 minutes by car from the main resort entrance, one of the shortest transfers of any major Caribbean resort airport.

Q: Which airlines operate at LRM?
A: The airport is primarily served by seasonal and charter carriers from the US, Canada, and Europe, with some scheduled service depending on the season.

Q: Is the airport close to any major tourist attractions?
A: Yes, the nearby Altos de Chavón replica Mediterranean village and the ports for Saona and Catalina Island excursions are all within a short drive.

Q: Does the airport have customs and immigration facilities?
A: Yes, LRM is an international airport with full customs and immigration services for arriving international passengers.
transport_tips: Pre-arranged resort transfers and taxis are readily available outside the terminal, with most resorts including pickup in their packages. Rental car agencies serve the airport if you plan to explore the region independently, though having a car is not essential given the proximity to Casa de Campo. Local gua-guas (public minibuses) and motoconchos pass along the main road if you want a budget-friendly option into La Romana town.
local_tip: Pack a lightweight change of clothes in your carry-on—after the short hop from the runway to the resort, you can hit the pool or the beach at Casa de Campo within 30 minutes of landing, well before your checked luggage arrives at the room.
